newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end lower after choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end lower after choppy trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures retreated from a midsession rally to finish lower as a technical short covering surge failed to attract outside buying interest, traders said.

Lumber started lower on reports of continued slow cash trade and then rallied after filling a gap in the charts. But technical demand lacked follow through after prices climbed to net gains and futures slipped again late, they said.
Prudential Securities, Saul Stone and Refco were on both sides of the market early with Refco and locals selling late, pit sources said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spuruce at $405 per tbf, up $9.00 from last Friday.
Cash sources attributed much of the gain in cash to filling of holes in inventories which only lasted a couple of days late last week. Cash trade has been slow since, they said.
Lumber closed $5.90 to $1.60 per thousand board feet lower with March off most at $407.30 and May down $2.90 at $382.90 per tbf.
